full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 11-7-91 passed by the District Judge, Jessore, in Title Appeal No. 36 of 1989 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 12-1-89 passed by the Assistant Judge, Jessore, in Title Suit No. 197 of 1986. 

 7. Against the said judgment and decree of the learned District Judge the plaintiff petitioners moved this application in revision and obtained the present Rule. 

 11. It is an established principle of Mohammadan Law that a gift is not liable to be revoked by the donor after delivery of possession, if it is made to a donee who is related to the donor within the prohibited degree. And once possession is delivered nothing short of a decree of a Court is sufficient for the revocation of a gift. 

 (4) Once possession is delivered, nothing short of a decree of the Court is sufficient to revoke the gift. Neither a declaration of revocation by the donor nor even the institution of a suit for resuming the gift is sufficient to revoke the gift. Until a decree is passed, the donee is entitled to use and dispose of the subject of the gift." 

 13. Admittedly, in the present case no such decree was passed by any court. The donees are also related to the donor within the prohibited degrees.
